pr_title: Allow to cast in HLS format when using WebRTC
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

See the linked issue for background, but the long story short is that casting cameras is no longer possible once you enable the native WebRTC integration.

After further analysis, it turns out that casting were being blocked by a constant check, i.e. the camera is fully able to supply a stream in HLS format but since its main format was set to WebRTC it was failing early.

This PR makes this behavior more tolerant, while still retaining the original error handle for returning a helpful message.

The format check is not decisive any longer, but instead we try to fetch a stream URL in HLS format.

If it succeeds, it means the camera is capable of providing a HLS stream and therefore it can be casted

If it fails, we still check for the original error for the sake of hinting the user on why it probably failed.

It's working normally on my main Home Assistant instance.

/cc @allenporter @dermotduffy

pr_comments: Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`camera`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L176) for? Thanks!

Hello, this does not address what I said in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/79494#issuecomment-1264718979

The issue is not just how to get this working, but about the technical decisions around the entity model.

I truly understand, and I wish that WebRTC streaming gets implemented. If it gets implemented, I believe streaming with both formats will have no use.

But nevertheless this is a short-term, harmless workaround that allow people to continue streaming in HLS format while using WebRTC, until the definitive solution gets implemented (which I'm assuming won't be soon).

Let me elaborate since I think it may not be clear based on your response: The first part of what I said is that there needs to be an architecture discussion to change the rules of the entity model. This is what I meant above by "The issue is not just how to get this working, but about the technical decisions around the entity model."
@balloob since you added this guard, curious for your hot take.

issue_context.title: No longer possible to cast camera after enabling RTSPToWebRTC
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I can no longer possible to cast  camera to chromecast after enabling RTSPToWebRTC integration. It fails with:

```
Failed to call service media_player/play_media. Camera does not support MJPEG or HLS streaming.
```

If I disable the RTSPToWebRTC it works just fine.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.9.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

RTSPToWebRTC

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rtsp_to_webrtc

### Diagnostics information

[config_entry-rtsp_to_webrtc-5ea4ba7a671b7d79d1d85ce227a54e08.json.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/9693269/config_entry-rtsp_to_webrtc-5ea4ba7a671b7d79d1d85ce227a54e08.json.txt)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I understand the Chromecast does not accept WebRTC streams, but Home Assistant should be smart enough to fallback to the HLS stream in such situation.

Hey there @allenporter, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`rtsp_to_webrtc`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L953) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

[rtsp_to_webrtc source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/rtsp_to_webrtc)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

This is really a feature request for cast to support WebRTC. (feature requests can go in forums)

(There is no intention to support both RTSP/HLS streams and WebRTC streams at the same time)

Woark arounds are:
-  sticking with LL-HLS (not using webrtc) if you want to support cast
-  cast a lovelace panel with a WebRTC card

> This is really a feature request for cast to support WebRTC. (feature requests can go in forums)

It is not, although that would be cool too.

> (There is no intention to support both RTSP/HLS streams and WebRTC streams at the same time)

I think falling back to HLS while WebRTC support in casting isn't implemented is fair. Does it mean that PRs for doing what I suggested won't be accepted either?

Here is the feature request by the way:

- https://community.home-assistant.io/t/cast-support-while-using-rtsptowebrtc/468623

I think this might require an architecture discussion e.g. similar to https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/640 -- explicitly this was discussed in https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/640#discussioncomment-1419962 as something not supported (supporting both stream types) so you'd have to propose how this should be interpreted in the entity model.

This is why i'm saying its not going to happen, and that really i'm saying its a feature request to make webrtc and cast work together.  Note there are cameras that support native webrtc also that would benefit from this.

Just one update, if I comment out the following 2 lines:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29582865/196803751-d0cd2efc-b0b9-4d66-8036-7af024a6c000.png)

The stream seems to work correctly (using HLS instead of WebRTC, even with WebRTC enabled).
